ledger.sentence: The WHO released its Global status report on cancer 2026 on 8 July 2026.
The WHO says annual new cancer cases could rise to nearly 35 million by 2050 without urgent action.
It estimates about 20.6 million new cases and close to 10 million deaths each year at present.
The report makes seven recommendations across three shifts: better capabilities, better protections and better value.
On 8 July 2026 the World Health Organization (WHO) published its Global status report on cancer 2026 and called for urgent action.
The WHO says cancer now causes an estimated 20.6 million new cases and close to 10 million deaths a year, making it the second leading cause of death worldwide after cardiovascular disease.
Without urgent action, it projects annual new cases rising to nearly 35 million by 2050.
The WHO says nearly four in ten cancer cases are linked to preventable risk factors.
ledger.note: Search 25 (also WHO 3 Feb 2026 'Four in ten cancer cases could be prevented globally').

ledger.sentence: The report sets out seven recommendations grouped under three shifts: better capabilities, better protections and better value.
It points to underinvestment in prevention, unequal access to diagnosis and treatment, and insufficient social protection.
The WHO's first global survey of people affected by cancer, with more than 4,000 respondents in 116 countries, found widespread psychological distress among patients and caregivers.
